institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Other areas of scientific research, and the possibility to do a master's project about something else than offered at KU.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The pandemic definitely affected it, but it was overall very good.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite okay, the UiT website was okay, and I believe that we received the information that we needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None, but didn't ask for it either.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The mobility team at UiT can be very slow with replying, and not always providing the best or most informative answers

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is quite easy. However, the prices are high and the standard are not always the best as many of the houses and apartments are quite old and not renovated. If you have the chance, go look at the different houses prior to accepting.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Make sure that you look at the possibility to get to the university from the housing, the distances can be long, and the buses connections are not the best.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Facebook groups,
finn.no
and
hybel.no
are great websites to look for housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Quite easy, and straight forward, but again, the mobility team-response was not super. And - if you decide to do something a little bit different, such as doing a project in stead of a course, if can be a little more complicated and will take some more time to fix

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Student info desk and mobility team

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing special, but remember that you can always ask them if you have any questions

questions.answer: Food is quite expensive, as well as alcohol of course

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The sports groups here are great, cheap and open for everyone!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of sports, and quite a lot of smaller social activities

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the sports groups! I joined the one for sailing, diving, ski touring, hiking, and surfing. Most of the groups are open for people at all levels, arrange different trips, and do a lot of fun stuff together

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the nature!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Again, join some of the sports groups

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That people here appreciate the nature and outdoors a lot!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Bring WARM clothes - Wool and Gore-Tex will be your new best friends
2) Tromsø city might not be the most exciting thing, but the nature compensates for that times 1000 
3) Try a new sport here - Tromsø is a great place to try something out of your comfort zone or a sport you always wanted to try

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Wool. Wool is your best friend. Wool everything. I will say it again: Wool.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I met a ton of great people, experienced nature in the best ways possible, and of course, was able to do research with some great scientists.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: All of the days with bad weather...

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: A tiny tip for the people staying here during the polar night: a wake-up lamp will be your next best friend after wool.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
